title: Before and after
job: Time clauses: while, until, since, already, not yet
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: The particle an is what turns a preposition into a conjunction: qabla an, baʿda an, ilā an. L3-M1's qabla and baʿda took a noun; with an behind them a whole verb clause follows.

qabla an always takes a present-shaped verb, even when the sentence around it is past: qabla an adhhab ilā al-ʿamal, sharibtu al-qahwa. What has not happened yet cannot be past, and that stays true when the not-yet sits inside a memory.

baʿda an takes the PAST when the event is past: baʿda an akaltu, dhahabtu ilā al-maktab. The two conjunctions are built alike and differ in what follows them, and the difference is real rather than stylistic.
ḥattā, until, takes a present-shaped verb for something still ahead — ḥattā yaṣil al-qiṭār — and a past for something reached: ḥattā waṣala al-qiṭār. ilā an does the same job and swaps with it.
athnāʾ and khilāl are the NOMINAL while, and the shape a careful speaker uses: each takes al- plus a noun or a maṣdar and never a verb — athnāʾ al-ijtimāʿ, khilāl al-akl.
English while covers a stretch and a point alike. Arabic splits them, and the split is already yours: L3-M10's baynamā for a stretch, ʿindamā for a point, and ḥīna naming the moment.
ALREADY is L3-M7's qad in front of a past verb — qad waṣaltu — and nothing new. NOT YET is lam plus the jussive with baʿd at the end of the clause: lam yaṣil baʿd.

baʿd, yet, and baʿda, after, differ by one written vowel. baʿd closes a clause and takes nothing; baʿda opens one and takes a noun or the particle an. Read the vowel or you will write baʿda at the end of a clause.

English drops the subject of a time clause — before going out, after eating. Arabic must have a finite verb with a person on it: qabla an adhhab, before I go. This is the same mismatch L4-M1 met with li-.
English since is one word for a start-point and for a reason. L3-M7's mundhu is only the start-point — adrus al-ʿarabiyya mundhu sana — and the reason word is L4-M2's.

sentences.display: qabla an adhhab ilā al-ʿamal, sharibtu al-qahwa
sentences.script: قبل أن أذهب إلى العمل، شربت القهوة
sentences.cue: Before I went to work, I drank coffee
sentences.literal: Before that I-go to the-work, I-drank the-coffee

words.note: L3-M1's qabla took a noun: qabla an-nawm. The particle an turns it into a conjunction and a whole verb clause follows.

sentences.trap: English agrees its tenses — before I WENT to work. Arabic does not: the verb after qabla an stays present-shaped however far in the past the sentence sits.
sentences.sound: QAB-la an ADH-hab: an is a light unstressed syllable that leans onto the verb; do not pause after it.

variations.display: qabla an anām, qaraʾtu al-kitāb
variations.script: قبل أن أنام، قرأت الكتاب
variations.cue: Before I slept, I read the book
variations.changed: the clause under qabla an: going to work becomes going to sleep

variations.display: qabla an adhhab ilā as-sūq, akaltu
variations.script: قبل أن أذهب إلى السوق، أكلت
variations.cue: Before I went to the market, I ate
variations.changed: where the first clause goes, and a bare past alone in the second

mistake.display: qabla an dhahabtu ilā al-ʿamal, sharibtu al-qahwa
mistake.script: قبل أن ذهبت إلى العمل، شربت القهوة
mistake.why: A past verb after qabla an. What has not happened yet cannot be past, and that stays true inside a memory — the shape is adhhab even when the telling is.

sentences.usage: Putting two events of a past day in order, the earlier one second.
sentences.mnemonic: qabla an = before + a clause; the verb behind it never goes back.

sentences.display: baʿda an akaltu, dhahabtu ilā al-maktab
sentences.script: بعد أن أكلت، ذهبت إلى المكتب
sentences.cue: After I ate, I went to the office
sentences.literal: After that I-ate, I-went to the-office

words.note: The twin of qabla an, built the same way on L3-M1's baʿda — but this one takes the PAST when the event is past.

sentences.trap: The pair looks symmetrical and is not. qabla an takes a present-shaped verb and baʿda an takes a past one, and no English rule predicts which is which.
sentences.sound: BAʿ-da an a-KAL-tu: the ʿayn in baʿda is a squeeze in the throat, not the hamza catch of qabla an.

variations.display: baʿda an waṣala al-qiṭār, dhahabtu ilā al-bayt
variations.script: بعد أن وصل القطار، ذهبت إلى البيت
variations.cue: After the train arrived, I went home
variations.changed: a third-person subject inside the time clause

variations.display: baʿda an akaltu, dhahabnā ilā as-sūq
variations.script: بعد أن أكلت، ذهبنا إلى السوق
variations.cue: After I ate, we went to the market
variations.changed: we, not I, in the second clause — the two clauses need not share a subject

mistake.display: baʿda an ākul, dhahabtu ilā al-maktab
mistake.script: بعد أن آكل، ذهبت إلى المكتب
mistake.why: A present-shaped verb after baʿda an for an event that is over. The symmetry with qabla an is the trap: only qabla an holds the present.

sentences.usage: Telling a day in order, one clause hanging off the last.
sentences.mnemonic: baʿda an looks back, so its verb looks back too.

sentences.cue: I will wait here until the train arrives

words.note: until. A present-shaped verb behind it means the event is still ahead; a past verb means it was reached. Both are ordinary.
L2-M10's intaẓartu in the present, with L1-M6's sa- written joined in front of it.
The present of L2-M10's waṣala. No mood ending is written, so the shape after ḥattā and after lam is the same three letters.

sentences.trap: English puts a present tense after until for a future event too (until the train arrives), so this one transfers — but the trap is the past: Arabic really does switch to waṣala once the waiting is over.
sentences.sound: sa-an-ta-ZIR ḥat-TĀ: the doubled t in ḥattā is held, a beat longer than a single one.

variations.display: sa-antaẓir hunā ḥattā taṣil al-ḥāfila
variations.script: سأنتظر هنا حتى تصل الحافلة
variations.cue: I will wait here until the bus arrives
variations.changed: a feminine subject, so the verb takes the t- prefix

variations.display: antaẓir hunā ḥattā yaṣil al-mudīr
variations.script: أنتظر هنا حتى يصل المدير
variations.cue: I am waiting here until the manager arrives
variations.changed: the plain present without sa-, so the waiting is now

mistake.why: A past verb behind ḥattā for something that has not happened. The past is for a point already reached; the wait ahead needs yaṣil.

sentences.usage: Saying how long you will stay put.
sentences.mnemonic: ḥattā looks both ways: yaṣil ahead, waṣala behind.

sentences.cue: I waited until the train arrived

words.note: The third of the an conjunctions, and the plainest: L1-M4's ilā plus an. It swaps with ḥattā here with no change of meaning.

sentences.trap: English until is one word for both jobs. Arabic has two words that overlap — ḥattā and ilā an — and neither is the wrong one here.
sentences.sound: in-ta-ẓAR-tu i-lā an: the ẓ is a heavy d-like sound made with the tongue flat, not the light z of English.

variations.display: intaẓartu ḥattā waṣala al-qiṭār
variations.script: انتظرت حتى وصل القطار
variations.cue: I waited until the train arrived
variations.changed: ḥattā in place of ilā an — the same sentence, the other word

variations.display: intaẓartu ilā an waṣalat al-ḥāfila
variations.script: انتظرت إلى أن وصلت الحافلة
variations.cue: I waited until the bus arrived
variations.changed: a feminine past subject, so the verb takes -at

mistake.why: ilā with no an. Without the particle it is still the preposition to, and a verb cannot follow it — an is the whole hinge.

sentences.usage: Closing a wait that is already over.
sentences.mnemonic: ilā an = ilā plus the hinge; drop an and you are back to a preposition.

sentences.display: athnāʾ al-ijtimāʿ, saʾalanī al-mudīr ʿan al-ʿamal
sentences.script: أثناء الاجتماع، سألني المدير عن العمل
sentences.cue: During the meeting, the manager asked me about the work
sentences.literal: During the-meeting, he-asked-me the-manager about the-work

words.note: The nominal while: it takes al- plus a noun, never a verb. Where English says while we met, careful Arabic says during the meeting.

sentences.trap: English while attaches to a clause; athnāʾ cannot. Reaching for while and translating it word for word produces athnāʾ with a verb behind it, which is not a sentence.
sentences.sound: ath-NĀʾ: the th is the soft one of English thin, and the word ends on a hamza — a catch, not a vowel that trails off.

variations.display: athnāʾ al-akl, saʾalanī abī ʿan al-madrasa
variations.script: أثناء الأكل، سألني أبي عن المدرسة
variations.cue: During the meal, my father asked me about school
variations.changed: a maṣdar behind athnāʾ — L4-M1's al-akl, the eating

variations.display: khilāl al-ijtimāʿ, saʾalanī al-mudīr ʿan al-ʿamal
variations.script: خلال الاجتماع، سألني المدير عن العمل
variations.cue: During the meeting, the manager asked me about the work
variations.changed: khilāl for athnāʾ — the same slot, the same meaning

mistake.display: athnāʾ adhhab ilā al-ʿamal, sharibtu al-qahwa
mistake.script: أثناء أذهب إلى العمل، شربت القهوة
mistake.why: A verb behind athnāʾ. It is a preposition-shaped word and needs a noun; for a verb the sentence wants baynamā.

sentences.usage: The register a careful speaker uses for a stretch of time.
sentences.mnemonic: athnāʾ takes a thing, baynamā takes a doing.

sentences.cue: During the meal, I do not talk much

words.note: athnāʾ's twin, and interchangeable with it here. Both take al- plus a noun; neither takes a verb.
I talk, I speak with someone. No mood ending is written, so the plain present ends on the bare consonant.

sentences.trap: English during and while are two words for one idea and a learner picks by feel. Arabic picks by what follows: a noun after khilāl, a clause after baynamā.
sentences.sound: khi-LĀL: the kh is the rasp at the back of the throat, the same sound as in L1's akh.

variations.display: khilāl an-nawm, lā ataḥaddath
variations.script: خلال النوم، لا أتحدث
variations.cue: During sleep, I do not talk
variations.changed: L3-M1's maṣdar an-nawm behind khilāl

variations.display: athnāʾ al-akl, lā ataḥaddath kathīran
variations.script: أثناء الأكل، لا أتحدث كثيراً
variations.cue: During the meal, I do not talk much
variations.changed: athnāʾ for khilāl — the pair really is a swap

mistake.why: A verb behind khilāl. Like athnāʾ it wants the maṣdar — the eating, al-akl — not the I-eat.

sentences.usage: Saying what you do or avoid across a stretch of time.
sentences.mnemonic: khilāl and athnāʾ both eat nouns.

sentences.display: ḥīna dhahabtu ilā al-maktab, kāna al-mudīr hunāka
sentences.script: حين ذهبت إلى المكتب، كان المدير هناك
sentences.cue: When I went to the office, the manager was there
sentences.literal: At-the-time I-went to the-office, was the-manager there

words.note: A third word for when, beside L3-M10's ʿindamā and baynamā. It names the moment, and unlike athnāʾ it takes a clause.

sentences.trap: English when covers a point and a stretch alike, so a learner reaches for one word. Arabic has three and they are not free variants: ḥīna and ʿindamā mark a point, baynamā a stretch.
sentences.sound: ḤĪ-na: the ḥ is the breathy h made deep in the throat, not the light h of hunāka in the same sentence.

variations.display: ʿindamā dhahabtu ilā al-maktab, kāna al-mudīr hunāka
variations.script: عندما ذهبت إلى المكتب، كان المدير هناك
variations.cue: When I went to the office, the manager was there
variations.changed: L3-M10's ʿindamā for ḥīna — the everyday word for the same point

variations.display: baynamā kuntu fī al-maktab, waṣala al-mudīr
variations.script: بينما كنت في المكتب، وصل المدير
variations.cue: While I was at the office, the manager arrived
variations.changed: baynamā, and with it a stretch instead of a point

mistake.display: ḥīna fī al-maktab, kāna al-mudīr hunāka
mistake.script: حين في المكتب، كان المدير هناك
mistake.why: A bare prepositional phrase after ḥīna. English drops the verb of a time clause — when at the office — and Arabic cannot: a finite verb with a person on it is required.

sentences.usage: Pinning one past event to the moment of another.
sentences.mnemonic: ḥīna is the hour of it: a point, and a clause.

sentences.cue: The train has not arrived yet

words.note: L3-M4's lam with the jussive: one particle makes the whole past negative and the verb keeps its present shape.

words.cue: yet (at the end of a clause)
words.note: yet. It closes the clause and takes nothing. It is baʿda without its final vowel and is a different word — see S02.

sentences.trap: English has not arrived yet is three words of machinery. Arabic is lam in front and baʿd behind, and nothing in the middle changes.
sentences.sound: lam ya-ṢIL baʿd: baʿd ends on a hard stop after the ʿayn — no trailing -a, which is the whole difference from baʿda.

variations.display: lam yaṣil al-mudīr baʿd
variations.script: لم يصل المدير بعد
variations.cue: The manager has not arrived yet
variations.changed: the subject only — the frame holds still around it

variations.display: lam taṣil al-ḥāfila baʿd
variations.script: لم تصل الحافلة بعد
variations.cue: The bus has not arrived yet
variations.changed: a feminine subject, so the jussive takes the t- prefix

mistake.why: baʿda at the end of a clause. baʿda is the preposition after and needs a noun or an behind it; the yet word is baʿd, and the vowel is the only thing telling them apart.

sentences.usage: Reporting that something expected is still outstanding.
sentences.mnemonic: baʿda opens and takes something; baʿd closes and takes nothing.

sentences.display: qad waṣala al-qiṭār, wa lākin lam yaṣil ṣadīqī baʿd
sentences.script: قد وصل القطار، ولكن لم يصل صديقي بعد
sentences.cue: The train has already arrived, but my friend has not arrived yet
sentences.literal: Already he-arrived the-train, and but not he-arrives my-friend yet

words.note: L3-M7's qad in front of a past verb is already. Nothing new is being opened here; the frame is named so that its opposite, lam … baʿd, has something to stand against.

sentences.trap: English already and not yet are a pair of adverbs. Arabic answers with two unlike machines: a particle in front for already, and a negative plus a word at the end for not yet.
sentences.sound: qad WA-ṣa-la: qad is short and clipped, and the stress stays on the verb behind it.

variations.display: qad waṣaltu, wa lākin lam yaṣil ṣadīqī baʿd
variations.script: قد وصلت، ولكن لم يصل صديقي بعد
variations.cue: I have already arrived, but my friend has not arrived yet
variations.changed: the first person in the already half

variations.display: qad waṣala al-mudīr, wa lākin lam yabdaʾ al-ijtimāʿ baʿd
variations.script: قد وصل المدير، ولكن لم يبدأ الاجتماع بعد
variations.cue: The manager has already arrived, but the meeting has not started yet
variations.changed: a different pair of events in the same two halves

mistake.display: waṣala al-qiṭār qad, wa lākin lam yaṣil ṣadīqī baʿd
mistake.script: وصل القطار قد، ولكن لم يصل صديقي بعد
mistake.why: qad after the verb. It is a particle that only ever stands in front; the word that goes at the end of a clause is baʿd, and only in the negative half.

sentences.usage: Giving good news and bad news about the same wait.
sentences.mnemonic: qad in front = already; baʿd at the back = not yet.

sentences.display: qad waṣaltu ilā al-maktab, wa lākin lam yabdaʾ al-ijtimāʿ baʿd
sentences.script: قد وصلت إلى المكتب، ولكن لم يبدأ الاجتماع بعد
sentences.cue: I have already arrived at the office, but the meeting has not started yet
sentences.literal: Already I-arrived to the-office, and but not he-starts the-meeting yet

words.note: The present of L3-M10's bada'a. It ends on a hamza, and under lam it keeps exactly this shape.

sentences.trap: English needs a perfect on both halves — have arrived, has not started. Arabic marks the first with qad and a past, and the second with lam and a present shape, and the two halves look nothing alike.
sentences.sound: yab-DAʾ: the final hamza is a clean stop; the word does not trail into a vowel.

variations.display: qad waṣaltu ilā al-bayt, wa lākin lam yabdaʾ al-akl baʿd
variations.script: قد وصلت إلى البيت، ولكن لم يبدأ الأكل بعد
variations.cue: I have already arrived home, but the meal has not started yet
variations.changed: the pair of events, kept in the same frame

variations.display: qad waṣala al-mudīr, wa lākin lam abdaʾ baʿd
variations.script: قد وصل المدير، ولكن لم أبدأ بعد
variations.cue: The manager has already arrived, but I have not started yet
variations.changed: the first person under lam, with no subject noun at all

mistake.display: qad waṣaltu ilā al-maktab, wa lākin al-ijtimāʿ lam yabdaʾ baʿda
mistake.script: قد وصلت إلى المكتب، ولكن الاجتماع لم يبدأ بعدَ
mistake.why: baʿda again for baʿd. The clause is closed by baʿd; baʿda would leave the ear waiting for a noun that never comes.

sentences.usage: Reporting in when you are early and nothing has happened.
sentences.mnemonic: Two halves, two machines: qad + past, lam + present + baʿd.
